info.name: Fortis API - Business users
info.description:
Every business-user route of the Fortis backend (prefix `/api/v1`): sign-in and sessions, passwords, owner registration, the business, branches and terminals, roles, members, overrides and invitations. Fortis staff routes are in **Fortis API - Fortis staff**.

## Setup

1. Start the API with its services: `npm run dev:up`, `npm run db:migrate`, `npm run start:dev`.
2. Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:3000/api/v1`).
3. Set `email`, `password` and, for desktop, `terminalId`. An owner account comes from the provisioning flow (Fortis staff collection) and **03 Owner registration**.
4. Run **01 Sign in and session > Login (desktop)**. It stores the tokens and the business and branch ids that later requests use.

Emailed tokens (password reset, invitations, owner activation) must be copied from the email into variables; locally the emails are in the Mailpit inbox.

## Authentication

Collection auth is `Bearer {{accessToken}}`; public routes override it with *No Auth*. Tokens are obtained by the requests, never stored in this file.

## Checks

Every request checks the `X-Request-Id` header and, for errors, the `{ statusCode, error, message, requestId }` body. Each request adds its own status and body checks and stores the ids later requests need.

Requests marked *destructive* change real data (ending a membership, revoking an invitation, deleting a role); run them against test data only.

item.name: 00 Service
item.description: Requests that need no business context.

request.description: Public liveness text. Health endpoints (`/health/live`, `/health/ready`) are not implemented yet.
Signed-in stub: accepts any JSON object and answers 202 `{ acknowledged, message }`. Not part of a product flow yet.

item.name: 01 Sign in and session
item.description:
Business users (owners and staff). Run **Login** first: it stores `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `userId`, `businessId` and `branchId`.

- Access tokens last 15 minutes; refresh tokens rotate on every refresh.
- Refresh **single-flight**: replaying an already-rotated refresh token is treated as theft and signs the account out everywhere.
- Native clients (`desktop`, `android_pos`, `mobile`) get both tokens in the body. Browsers (`web`, `web_terminal`) get the refresh token only as the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (Postman keeps it in its cookie jar).

header.description: web, web_terminal, desktop, android_pos or mobile. Native clients get the refresh token in the body; web gets it as an httpOnly cookie.
Required for every client type except web: an active terminal in the member's business and branch.

request.description:
Signs in with email and password. `remember: true` gives a 30-day refresh session, otherwise 12 hours.

**Prerequisites:** an active account with an active membership; for non-web clients, `terminalId` of an active terminal in that business and branch.

**Errors:** 400 invalid body or headers, 401 wrong credentials or terminal (same message for unknown emails), 429 rate limited (strict throttle).

Browser sign-in: `x-terminal-id` is optional, the access token is in the body, and the refresh token is only set as the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (path `/api/v1/authentication`, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production). `remember: false` makes it a browser-session cookie.

This request does not overwrite the stored `refreshToken`; the desktop requests keep using theirs.

request.description:
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token. Native clients send `refreshToken` in the body; browsers send nothing and rely on the cookie.

Run it once per stored token: sending the same token twice is reuse detection and revokes every session.

**Errors:** 401 unknown, expired, revoked or reused token (clears the cookie); 429 rate limited.

item.name: 02 Passwords
item.description:
Password rules: 10 to 128 characters. Reset links are emailed (local stack: the Mailpit inbox) and work once within 30 minutes.
Copy the `token` query parameter of the emailed link into the `resetToken` variable before running **Reset password**.

header.description: web, web_terminal, desktop, android_pos or mobile. Native clients get the refresh token in the body; web gets it as an httpOnly cookie.

request.description:
Requires the current password. Signs out every device and returns a new session (same shape as login). The test swaps `password` and `newPassword`, so running it again changes the password back.

**Errors:** 400 missing current password or unchanged password, 403 wrong current password, 429 rate limited.
Always answers 202 with the same message, whether or not the email has an account, so it reveals nothing. Active accounts get a reset link (at most one new link per minute).

**Prerequisite:** `resetToken` from the emailed link (`.../reset-password?token=...`).

Sets the new password and signs the account out everywhere; sign in again afterwards. The test moves `newPassword` into `password`.

**Errors:** one generic 400 for any unusable token.

item.name: 03 Owner registration
item.description: The first owner of a business that Fortis staff provisioned. The redeem code, business, branch and terminal code arrive in the owner-activation email.

request.description:
Creates the owner account (or verifies the password of an existing one), adds the owner membership and activates the business. Issues no tokens: sign in afterwards.

**Prerequisites:** values from the owner-activation email in `redeemCode`, `businessId`, `branchId`, `terminalCode`.

**Errors:** 400 invalid data; 401 invalid, expired or used code, or wrong password for an existing account; 409 already activated or already a member; 429 rate limited.

item.name: 04 Business, branches and terminals
item.description: Every route needs a permission in the business (`:businessId`), checked in the database. Denials are one generic 403; a malformed id is 400.

request.description: **Permission:** `business:read`. Business profile and activation state.

header.description: Required. Reusing a key with the same payload replays the first response for 7 days; with a different payload it is 409.

request.description:
**Permission:** `business:update`. Multipart: profile fields plus optional replacement documents. PAN, legal name and status cannot be changed (422). Audited.

**Errors:** 403, 409 idempotency conflict, 422 prohibited or no fields.

formdata.description: Optional document, up to 10 MB. Set the file in Postman.

request.description: **Permission:** `branch:read`. Keyset pagination. Members limited to a branch see only their branch.
**Permission:** `branch:read` at this branch. Branch plus terminal and member counts. **Errors:** 403 another branch of a branch-limited member, 404 out of scope.

**Permission:** `terminal:activate` at this branch. Activates an inactive terminal by its emailed code (case-insensitive). Repeating it for an active terminal returns it unchanged. Audited.

**Errors:** 404 unknown business, branch or code; 409 terminal cannot be activated.

item.name: 05 Roles and permissions
item.description: System roles (admin, branch-manager, cashier, inventory-manager, accountant, viewer) are shared and read-only. Custom roles belong to one business. Nobody can put a permission into a role that they do not hold themselves.

request.description: Signed-in users. Every permission code with its description.
**Permission:** `role:read`. System roles plus this business's roles, with their permissions. Stores the cashier and viewer role ids.

**Permission:** `role:create` (business-wide members). Body: `name`, optional `description`, optional `branchId` (limits the role to that branch, fixed afterwards), `permissions`. The `key` is derived from the name.

**Errors:** 400 unknown code or branch, 403 granting a permission you lack, 409 duplicate name.
**Permission:** `role:read`.

**Permission:** `role:update`. Only the fields sent change; an empty `description` clears it. `version` increases on every edit. You can only edit a role whose permissions you all hold.

**Errors:** 403 system role or a role granting something you lack, 409 duplicate name.
**Permission:** `role:delete`. **Errors:** 403 system role, 404 unknown, 409 still assigned to active members or open invitations.

item.name: 06 Members and overrides
item.description: Business-wide member management. Overrides grant (`allow`) or remove (`deny`) one permission for one member; deny wins.

request.description: **Permission:** `member:read`. Active members.  Stores the first member who is neither you nor the owner as `memberUserId`.
**Permission:** `member:read`. Includes overrides and effective permissions.

**Permission:** `member:update`. Body: `roleId` and/or `branchId` (`branchId: null` = business-wide). Moving someone to another branch signs them out.

Refused (403): changing yourself or the owner; managing someone who holds a permission you lack; assigning a role that grants something you lack; on branch routes, moving someone out of the branch. Other branches' members are 404 on branch routes.

**Permission:** `override:manage` (business-wide). `effect` is `allow` or `deny`. You can only allow a permission you hold yourself.

**Errors:** 400 unknown permission, 403 escalation or self/owner, 404 member not found.
**Permission:** `override:manage`. Lifting a deny counts as granting: you must hold the permission. **Errors:** 404 no such override.

**Permission:** `member:end`. Ends the membership, removes the member's overrides and signs them out everywhere. Run it only against a test member.

**Errors:** 403 (same rules as changing a member), 404 no active membership in scope.

item.name: 07 Invitations
item.description: Business-wide invitations. The raw token is only ever in the email; the API stores its hash.

request.description:
**Permission:** `member:invite`. Up to 20 addresses with one role (and optional `branchId`). Answers 200 with one status per address: `invited`, `already_member`, `already_invited`, `invalid` or `forbidden` (the role grants something you lack). 

Each invited address gets an email with a single-use link (`.../invitations/accept?token=...`), valid for 7 days.
**Permission:** `member:read`. Latest 200 with status `open`, `expired`, `accepted` or `revoked`. Stores the newest open invitation as `invitationId`.
**Permission:** `member:invite`. Issues a new token and expiry and emails it; the previous link stops working. **Errors:** 404 no open invitation.
**Permission:** `member:invite`. **Errors:** 404 no open invitation.

item.name: 08 Branch-scoped management (branch managers)
item.description:
The same member and invitation routes under `/businesses/{{businessId}}/branches/{{branchId}}/`. The permission is checked **at that branch**, only that branch's members and invitations are visible, and people can only be placed in that branch.

Members limited to one branch (for example a branch manager) must use these routes: business-wide checks fail for them except reading the business, its branches and its roles. Sign in as a branch manager to see the difference; the owner can use them too.

request.description: **Permission:** `member:read`. Active members. Only members of this branch. Stores the first member who is neither you nor the owner as `memberUserId`.
**Permission:** `member:read`. Includes overrides and effective permissions.

**Permission:** `member:update`. Body: `roleId` and/or `branchId` (`branchId: null` = business-wide). Moving someone to another branch signs them out.

Refused (403): changing yourself or the owner; managing someone who holds a permission you lack; assigning a role that grants something you lack; on branch routes, moving someone out of the branch. Other branches' members are 404 on branch routes.

**Permission:** `member:end`. Ends the membership, removes the member's overrides and signs them out everywhere. Run it only against a test member.

**Errors:** 403 (same rules as changing a member), 404 no active membership in scope.

**Permission:** `member:invite`. Up to 20 addresses with one role (and optional `branchId`). Answers 200 with one status per address: `invited`, `already_member`, `already_invited`, `invalid` or `forbidden` (the role grants something you lack). On this route the branch is always this branch; a different `branchId` in the body is 400.

Each invited address gets an email with a single-use link (`.../invitations/accept?token=...`), valid for 7 days.
**Permission:** `member:read`. Latest 200 with status `open`, `expired`, `accepted` or `revoked`. Stores the newest open invitation as `invitationId`.
**Permission:** `member:invite`. Issues a new token and expiry and emails it; the previous link stops working. **Errors:** 404 no open invitation.
**Permission:** `member:invite`. **Errors:** 404 no open invitation.

item.name: 09 Invitation links (public)
item.description:
What the invitee does with the emailed link. Copy the `token` query parameter into `invitationToken`.

Accepting is single use. A person who is an active member of another business must send `confirmResignation: true` (ending that membership and signing them out there); an owner of another business can never accept.

request.description: Business, role, branch, expiry, and whether the email already has an account. **Errors:** 400 malformed token, 404 unusable invitation.

For an email without an account: sets the name and a password (10 to 128 characters). Response: `{ businessId, userId, accountCreated }`; sign in afterwards.

**Errors:** 400 any unusable token or missing name; 409 active elsewhere without confirmation, or owner of another business.

For an email that already has an account: send that account's password. `confirmResignation: true` is needed only when the person is active at another business.

**Errors:** 400 wrong password or unusable token; 409 without confirmation, or owner of another business.

header.description: web, web_terminal, desktop, android_pos or mobile. Native clients get the refresh token in the body; web gets it as an httpOnly cookie.

request.description: Public (works with an expired access token). Revokes the session of the given refresh token (or the cookie for web) and clears the cookie. Always 204.
Revokes every session of the signed-in user. Response: `{ revoked }` (count).
